Summary: The PC is taking longer to start, especially after a recent Steam-related startup change.
likely_cause: Steam and its associated programs are now starting with Windows, adding to boot time.
Evidence: On startup, the PC took 152 seconds on Saturday, matching a recent change.
Steam and two related items were added to startup on Wednesday.
Previous slow startups (141 seconds) occurred after similar changes.
No resource spikes or hardware issues were recorded during boot.
Steps: Open Task Manager and go to the 'Startup' tab.
Find Steam or any related programs listed there.
Right-click each and select 'Disable' to stop them from starting with Windows.
Restart the PC and check if startup time improves.
